episode_title: The Other Side Of The Bed: Humanizing Patients Beyond The Chart With Dr. Stella Awua-Larbi

real_qa.q: What inspired Dr. Stella Awua-Larbi to shift from biochemistry to medicine during her undergraduate years?
real_qa.r: Dr. Awua-Larbi was volunteering in the emergency room with a friend when she began transporting patients from the ER to imaging. While transporting them, she started having conversations with patients about their lives and families rather than just their medical conditions. She felt comfortable in that setting and realized it was the human connection that drew her to medicine. After that experience, she went to her advisor and said she knew exactly what she wanted to do: become a doctor based on her appreciation for the human connection in clinical settings.
real_qa.requete: Stella Awua-Larbi medicine career shift biochemistry

real_qa.q: How did Dr. Stella Awua-Larbi's perspective on patient care change after encountering a young patient labeled as non-compliant and difficult?
real_qa.r: Dr. Awua-Larbi encountered a patient in her 20s labeled as non-compliant and difficult in her chart who refused to answer questions. After reflecting on the patient's history, she learned the patient had been sick since age four and was in and out of hospitals. Dr. Awua-Larbi realized that as a mother, if her own daughter had been diagnosed with chronic illness at age four, she would raise her in fear, survival mode, and worry about hospital readmissions. This shifted her expectation: instead of expecting the patient to change, she changed herself and began incorporating deeper social history questions to understand the human story behind every medical chart.
real_qa.requete: The Other Side of the Bed humanizing patients Dr. Stella

real_qa.q: What is the core message of Dr. Stella Awua-Larbi's book 'The Other Side of the Bed'?
real_qa.r: The book's core message is that minimizing labeling is essential because you cannot discover someone through a label. While labeling can feel protective, it restricts the whole life underneath that label. Dr. Awua-Larbi emphasizes that the principles apply across humanity—in education, caregiving, and personal relationships. The book uses hospital-based cases and her own clinical experience, but ultimately the message is for all of humanity: understanding that behind every label or medical chart there is a human story that explains not only attitude but also physical and mental status.
real_qa.requete: The Other Side of the Bed Dr. Stella book meaning

real_qa.q: How did Dr. Stella Awua-Larbi find time to write her debut book while working as a nephrologist and managing her family responsibilities?
real_qa.r: Dr. Awua-Larbi had been collecting life lessons and stories for years through diary entries and Facebook posts, mostly reflecting on difficult patient encounters. When she turned 50, she set a specific goal to do something purposeful beyond her daily physician work and share her experiences. She woke up very early in the morning and dedicated 30 minutes to one hour after work consistently starting in the fall, using the already-collected stories as her foundation. This disciplined approach, combined with support from a great editor, enabled her to complete the book.
real_qa.requete: Dr. Stella Awua-Larbi writing book process schedule

real_qa.q: What self-care practice does Dr. Stella Awua-Larbi use to manage stress during difficult days in her medical practice?
real_qa.r: Dr. Awua-Larbi's self-care is a small quiet room or prayer room that fits only a two-seater couch, decorated with pink artificial flowers and a small lamp. She has set a boundary where her family knows not to disturb her when she enters this space. She spends 15 to 30 minutes or longer sitting, praying, listening to music that speaks to her heart, or simply being quiet. The room has two Bible verses on the wall—'Be still and know I'm God' and another about not being anxious—which remind her that everything will be okay.
real_qa.requete: Dr. Stella Awua-Larbi self-care prayer room practice

guest.bio_context: Dr. Stella Awua-Larbi was born and raised in Tema, Ghana, and moved to the United States at age 19 in January 1996 to Wisconsin without knowing anyone. She initially pursued a biochemistry major at the University of Wisconsin-Madison with plans to study food science like her father, but pivoted to medicine after volunteering in an emergency room and discovering her passion for human connection with patients. She is a nephrologist with 25+ years of clinical experience, a mother of two children (one in college, one a junior in high school), and published her debut book 'The Other Side of the Bed' at age 50.
